summary: Gemma 4's dense vision attention omitted its already-known host max sequence length, forcing the ROCm Triton vision backend to recover it from a GPU tensor with .item() in every encoder block at the function named in the reported watchdog stack. The change forwards seq_len as max_seqlen. Contract regressions fail before and pass after; the real gfx950 Triton path agrees with an independent PyTorch SDPA reference. The original Gemma-4-31B-it TP=8 server hang was not reproduced because this job has one GPU and no model weights.

tests.what_was_measured: Both single-item and batched Gemma 4 forwarding regressions failed because max_seqlen was absent; raw output: reports/j-ad639cc3195c/raw/regression-before.txt

Nine tests passed, covering Gemma 4 single-item and batched forwarding plus existing precomputed-max contracts for Triton, FA3, FA4, and MoonViT; raw output: reports/j-ad639cc3195c/raw/focused-tests-after.txt

On AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950, dense cases (bsz=1, seq_len=7) and (bsz=3, seq_len=5) matched torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention with maximum absolute errors 0.00081396 and 0.00091529; raw output: reports/j-ad639cc3195c/raw/gfx950-triton-numerical.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: One assigned AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950) executed the actual VisionTritonAttention kernel for two dense-shape cases; see reports/j-ad639cc3195c/raw/gfx950-triton-numerical.txt

remaining_limitations: Only one gfx950 GPU was assigned, so TP=8 collective behavior and the reported eight-GPU PCIe topology were not reproduced.
Gemma-4-31B-it weights were unavailable, so full model loading, multimodal preprocessing, hybrid SWA allocation, HTTP readiness, and semantic output were not tested.
The GPU fixture validates the implicated Triton attention execution and numerical output only; it does not prove that every possible cause of the original distributed hang is removed.
No native C++ or FlyDSL source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
